Reduce redundant ion features and annotate their relationships

mc_filter_ms.Rd

Apply isotope, adduct, neutral-loss, in-source-fragment, mispicked-ion, and ringing-artifact filters. Retain representative features and expose the annotation tables for inspection.

mc_filter_ms(x, filters = NULL, parameters = mc_ms_parameters(),
    adducts = NULL, neutral_losses = NULL, spectra = NULL)

Arguments

x

A metabocensor_result returned by mc_prepare() or a filtering function.

filters

Any of "isotopes", "adducts", "neutral_losses", "isf", "mispicked", and "ringing". An explicit vector overrides enable flags in parameters. NULL uses those flags; isotopes and adducts are enabled by default. character(0) disables all subfilters.

parameters

Named list from mc_ms_parameters(). Pass your list explicitly with parameters = ms_options.

adducts

Custom adduct data frame or local CSV filename. NULL uses built-in definitions. Required columns are described below.

neutral_losses

Custom neutral-loss data frame or local CSV filename. NULL uses built-in definitions. Required columns are described below.

spectra

A Spectra object, for example from mc_read_mgf(). Required for ISF when MS2 checking is enabled.

Details

Filters run in this order, irrespective of their order in filters:

isotopes

Find candidate isotope/dimer-pattern mass shifts within retention-time and Pearson-correlation thresholds. Connected families retain their highest-mean-intensity feature.

adducts

Convert candidate ion forms to neutral-mass intervals and connect compatible features within retention-time and correlation tolerances. Optional strict retention-time control limits family-wide RT spread. By default, each family retains its highest mean intensity feature. Optionally prefer selected ion forms within a specified percentage of the family's highest mean intensity. Retain the most intense qualifying preferred feature, or the most intense feature overall if none qualify.

neutral_losses

Find correlated, coeluting pairs separated by a listed neutral-loss mass. Remove the lower-m/z member of accepted pairs.

isf

Find correlated, coeluting lower-m/z candidate fragments, optionally constrained by fragment-to-precursor intensity ratio. With MS2 checking enabled, require the candidate fragment mass in a matching precursor spectrum above the relative-intensity threshold. A match in any eligible spectrum for that precursor is sufficient. Remove accepted lower-m/z fragments.

mispicked

Group nearly coincident, correlated features. Keep the highest-mean-intensity representative and sum family intensities into it for each sample.

ringing

Identify lower-intensity, correlated signals near a sufficiently intense anchor, subject to m/z, RT, and intensity-ratio limits; remove accepted artifacts.

Pearson correlations and mean intensities are computed across all sample columns in the input object. The MS step does not select samples by group label. Each subfilter receives the features remaining after the preceding subfilter.

Adduct tables require Name, Charge, Mult, and Mass; optional Ion_mode selects positive or negative entries. Neutral mass is calculated as (mz - Mass) * abs(Charge) / Mult. If required adduct columns are missing, a warning is issued and built-in definitions are used.

Neutral-loss tables require Accurate Mass and Neutral Loss. Optional Pos and Neg columns restrict definitions by polarity; Formula and substructure or compound class provide extra annotations.

Use isf_ms2_check2 = FALSE explicitly for MS1-only ISF filtering. Otherwise provide spectra with IDs matching the peak table. See mc_ms_parameters() for all tolerances and switches.

Each filtering stage can be used once per result object. To change its settings, start again from the object saved before that stage. Separate stages may be called in any order; each receives only the features retained so far.

Value

The updated result with retained table, removed_ids$ms, and updated counts. ms$counts reports sequential removal counts by subfilter; ms$isf_status records ISF processing status.

annot_tbls contains iso_table, add_table, nl_table, isf_table, mis_table, and ring_table. These tables describe feature relationships, masses/retention times, correlation evidence, and retention status where applicable. Tables may be NULL when a step is disabled or yields no annotation table; inspect names before subsetting columns. Annotation rows are not necessarily one row per removed feature.

merge_map records mispicked-feature merges when produced. Spectra are not stored in the result; keep the supplied Spectra object for later export.

See also

mc_ms_parameters, mc_read_mgf, mc_plot_ms, mc_export

Examples

if (FALSE) {
# The peak table and labels are bundled; only MGF requires internet.
peak_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "orbi_iimn_gnps_quant.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported <- mc_prepare(
  peak_file, type = "mzmine",
  sample_keywords = c(".mzML", "Peak area")
)
metadata_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_metadata(
  metadata_file, sample_names = imported$sample_cols,
  sample_col = "Sample name", label_col = "Label"
)
after_blank <- mc_filter_blank(
  imported, groups = "Blank", mode = "mean_cutoff", cutoff = 0.10
)
mgf_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plyush1993/",
  "MetaboCensoR_Examples/main/orbi/orbi_iimn_gnps.mgf"
)
mgf_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".mgf")
download.file(mgf_url, mgf_file, mode = "wb")
spectra <- mc_read_mgf(mgf_file)
ms_options <- mc_ms_parameters(
  iso_rt2 = 0.01, iso_cor2 = 0.80,
  iso_tol_type2 = "da", iso_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  add_rt2 = 0.005, add_cor2 = 0.80,
  add_tol_type2 = "da", add_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  add_pol2 = "positive",
  isf_rt2 = 0.01, isf_cor2 = 0.95,
  isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE, isf_mgf_id_field = "acquisitionNum",
  isf_ms2_mz_tol2 = 0.01, isf_ms2_rel2 = 1
)
after_ms <- mc_filter_ms(
  after_blank, filters = c("isotopes", "adducts", "isf"),
  parameters = ms_options, spectra = spectra
)
after_ms$ms$counts
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$add_table)
head(after_ms$annot_tbls$isf_table)
}
